paintings.file: Granville Redmond - California poppy field.jpg
paintings.title: California Poppy Field
paintings.blurb: Redmond lost his hearing to scarlet fever as a toddler and trained at the California School for the Deaf in Berkeley before studying in Paris. Back home in Southern California he became famous for hillsides set ablaze with the state flower, and collectors couldn't get enough of them. He privately preferred his hushed tonalist nocturnes, but it was the poppies that paid the bills and made his name.
paintings.setting: The golden poppy blankets California's coastal ranges every spring, and Redmond returned to these glowing fields throughout his life.
paintings.alt: A sunlit field of brilliant orange poppies stretching toward low green hills under a soft blue sky.

paintings.file: Ansel Adams - National Archives 79-AA-G01.jpg
paintings.title: The Tetons and the Snake River
paintings.museum: U.S. National Archives (National Park Service Mural Project), Washington, D.C.
paintings.blurb: In 1941 the National Park Service hired Adams to photograph the parks for a giant mural in the Department of the Interior building. World War II ended the commission before a single mural was hung, but Adams kept working, and this is the picture that came home: the Snake River curling like a silver ribbon toward a wall of storm-lit peaks. A print of it now rides aboard the Voyager spacecraft, a sample of Earth carried into interstellar space.
paintings.setting: Adams made his name in California's High Sierra, and this federal commission is squarely public domain — the cleanest, freest body of his work.
paintings.alt: A black-and-white view of a wide river bending through a dark evergreen valley toward jagged, snow-streaked mountains under a dramatic sky.

paintings.file: The Mowers (When Hearts Beat as One) by Granville Redmond.JPG
paintings.title: The Mowers (When Hearts Beat as One)
paintings.blurb: Painted at the height of Redmond's tonalist period, this quiet scene trades his trademark poppies for the gentler poetry of farm labor at day's end. Two figures move through a golden field as warm light settles over the land. Redmond, a close friend of Charlie Chaplin who taught the actor sign language, had a gift for stillness — and here it turns an ordinary harvest into something almost reverent.
paintings.setting: California's working countryside was as much Redmond's subject as its wildflowers; this canvas now hangs in San Francisco's de Young Museum.
paintings.alt: Two figures mowing in a glowing golden field, with soft hills and a hazy warm sky behind them.

paintings.file: Sierra Nevada Morning oil 1870 Albert Bierstadt.jpg
paintings.title: Sierra Nevada Morning
paintings.blurb: Morning light filters through mist into a deep Sierra valley, catching a waterfall, a herd of deer, and a glassy lake below jagged peaks. Bierstadt stitched these grand views together from field studies he made in the California high country, then amplified the drama in his New York studio. Critics sometimes scolded him for exaggeration, but it was exactly this golden, theatrical glow that thrilled audiences and helped sell the West to the nation.
paintings.setting: The scene distills the California Sierra at dawn — the range Bierstadt sketched on expedition and returned to throughout his career.
paintings.alt: A misty mountain valley at dawn, sunlight breaking over a waterfall and a lake with deer gathered along the near shore.

paintings.file: Albert Bierstadt - Scene in Yosemite Valley.jpg
paintings.title: Scene in Yosemite Valley
paintings.blurb: Bierstadt first reached Yosemite in 1863 and was overwhelmed — the sheer granite walls and falling water gave him a subject for the rest of his life. Here the valley opens in warm, hazy light, its cliffs softened by atmosphere and a quiet river threading the foreground. Paintings like this one carried Yosemite east to people who would never see it, and helped build the case for protecting it as public land.
paintings.setting: Yosemite Valley, in California's Sierra Nevada, was set aside by Congress in 1864 — the first land the U.S. ever protected expressly for public preservation.
paintings.alt: A broad mountain valley bathed in golden haze, with high granite cliffs, scattered trees, and a calm river in the foreground.

paintings.file: Granville Redmond - Coastal wildflowers.jpg
paintings.title: Coastal Wildflowers
paintings.blurb: Where his famous poppy fields blaze pure orange, here Redmond mixes the full spring palette — poppies threaded with lupine and other wildflowers spilling toward the sea. He worked these blooming hillsides again and again, chasing the few brilliant weeks each year when California's coast erupts in color before the summer gold sets in.
paintings.setting: Spring wildflower blooms along California's coastal hills were a lifelong subject for Redmond, who painted them from Laguna up the state.
paintings.alt: A coastal hillside carpeted in orange and purple wildflowers sloping down toward the ocean under a pale sky.

paintings.file: Albert Bierstadt - Mariposa Indian Encampment, Yosemite Valley, California.jpg
paintings.title: Mariposa Indian Encampment, Yosemite Valley, California
paintings.blurb: Beneath Yosemite's immense cliffs, Bierstadt sets a small encampment of the valley's Native people, their fire smoke drifting up into a luminous evening sky. The human figures are tiny against the granite and the glowing air — a favorite Bierstadt move that makes the landscape feel vast and sacred. The warm light gathering in the valley is the real subject, with the camp a tender note of life inside all that grandeur.
paintings.setting: Yosemite was the homeland of the Ahwahneechee people long before it drew painters and tourists; Bierstadt painted their presence into his California valley scenes.
paintings.alt: A Native encampment with figures and rising campfire smoke beneath towering cliffs, lit by a glowing golden evening sky.

paintings.file: Mountain Lake by Edgar Alwin Payne, Phoenix Art Museum.JPG
paintings.title: Mountain Lake
paintings.blurb: The High Sierra was to Payne what Mont Sainte-Victoire was to Cezanne — a peak he returned to over and over. Largely self-taught, he packed mules into the backcountry to paint granite faces and alpine lakes, working fast and finishing nearly a canvas a day. This still mountain lake, cupped beneath sheer rock, shows why his name became synonymous with the range.
paintings.setting: Payne, the first president of the Laguna Beach Art Association, made the alpine lakes of California's High Sierra the heart of his life's work.
paintings.alt: A glassy alpine lake mirroring tall granite peaks beneath a bright, cloud-streaked sky.

paintings.file: Alcatraz and the Golden Gate, San Francisco Bay, California, 1898-1905.jpg
paintings.title: Alcatraz and the Golden Gate, San Francisco Bay
paintings.blurb: Decades before color film, the Detroit Photographic Company turned black-and-white negatives into glowing color using a Swiss process called photochrom — hand-tinted stone plates that built up an image one hue at a time. The result reads like memory: softer and warmer than real life. Here the bay opens toward the strait that ships had long called the Golden Gate, the island of Alcatraz still an army fort, the famous bridge decades from being built.
paintings.setting: San Francisco Bay before the bridge that would later span the Golden Gate — a postcard view of California at the turn of the century.
paintings.alt: A color print of a calm bay with a rocky island at left, sailing ships on the water, and low golden hills meeting the sea in the distance.

paintings.file: Laguna Beach, by Edgar Alwin Payne.jpg
paintings.title: Laguna Beach
paintings.blurb: Payne first came to Laguna Beach in 1909 — and met his future wife, the painter Elsie Palmer, on that very trip. The couple later kept a studio on this stretch of coast, where Payne worked the surf and headlands that helped make Laguna an artists' colony. He and William Wendt were among the founders of its art association, with Payne serving as first president.
paintings.setting: Laguna Beach, on the Orange County coast, was both Payne's home base and the cradle of Southern California's plein air movement.
paintings.alt: Rocky coastal bluffs above a blue cove, with surf breaking against the rocks under a luminous sky.

paintings.file: View from Smiley's Heights, Redlands, Cal-LCCN2008678115.jpg
paintings.title: View from Smiley Heights, Redlands
paintings.blurb: At the turn of the century, Smiley Heights was one of Southern California's must-see sights — a hilltop pleasure garden the Smiley brothers planted above Redlands and opened to the public, threaded with carriage drives among palms, roses, and rare trees. From its terraces visitors looked clear across the orange-grove valley to snow on the San Bernardino Mountains. This photochrom sells exactly that promise: a manicured, semi-tropical California with winter peaks on the horizon.
paintings.setting: Redlands, in the citrus country east of Los Angeles, where the Smiley family's famous garden drew tourists by the trainload.
paintings.alt: A color view down a landscaped hillside of palms and flowering shrubs toward a green valley, with hazy mountains beyond under a soft sky.

paintings.file: Guy Rose - Carmel Dunes (c. 1918-20).jpg
paintings.title: Carmel Dunes
paintings.museum: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA), Los Angeles
paintings.blurb: Born in San Gabriel, Rose became the most 'French' of the California Impressionists — he lived in Giverny for years and counted Monet as a friend. Late in his career he and his wife summered in Carmel-by-the-Sea, and the empty dunes there gave him this image of pure solitude. The sky burns with an almost glaring brightness and the colors run high and saturated.
paintings.setting: Between 1918 and 1920 Rose painted as a summer resident of Carmel-by-the-Sea on California's Monterey coast; this canvas is now at LACMA.
paintings.alt: Rolling sand dunes spotted with scrub under a brilliant, glowing sky, with a hint of sea beyond.

paintings.file: Thomas Hill - Emerald Bay, Lake Tahoe (1864).jpg
paintings.title: Emerald Bay, Lake Tahoe
paintings.museum: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)
paintings.blurb: Hill paints the famous cove of Lake Tahoe in clear, bright light, its still water cupped by forested slopes and snow-touched peaks. Painted early in his California years, it shows the crisp realism and love of mountain detail that made his reputation. The bay's deep green color, which gives it its name, glows against the granite as a few small figures rest at the shore.
paintings.setting: Emerald Bay sits on the southwest shore of Lake Tahoe, the alpine lake straddling California and Nevada that drew Hill back through his career.
paintings.alt: A calm green mountain bay ringed by pine-covered slopes and distant snow peaks, with small figures resting on the rocky shore.

paintings.file: Mission Santa Barbara by Oriana Weatherbee Day.JPG
paintings.title: Mission Santa Barbara
paintings.museum: de Young Museum (Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco)
paintings.blurb: Oriana Day set out to paint all 21 of California's missions — only the second artist ever to attempt the whole chain — for a history book the Vallejo family never finished. She worked partly from memory and old accounts, so her canvases are gentle reconstructions of how the missions might once have looked. Santa Barbara, with its twin bell towers and neoclassical front, is often called the 'Queen of the Missions,' and Day paints it serene and sunhurried in the warm light of its coastal foothills.
paintings.setting: Mission Santa Barbara, founded in 1786, still stands above the city of Santa Barbara on California's central coast.
paintings.alt: A painting of a pale stone mission church with two bell towers and a columned façade, set among low hills under a soft blue sky.

paintings.file: Guy Rose, Off Mission Point (Point Lobos), n.d. Oil on canvas, 24 x 29 inches. Crocker Art Museum.jpg
paintings.title: Off Mission Point (Point Lobos)
paintings.blurb: Point Lobos, just south of Carmel, is one of the most painted headlands on the California coast, and Rose returned to it for its cypress, surf, and shifting fog. One curator called him as important to California as Monet was to France — high praise that his shimmering coastal light earns. The Crocker Art Museum now holds one of the country's great collections of his work.
paintings.setting: Point Lobos, on the Monterey Peninsula, drew Rose during his Carmel years for its dramatic meeting of rock, sea, and weather.
paintings.alt: A rugged rocky point meeting the open sea, surf foaming against the rocks under a soft blue-grey sky.

paintings.file: William Keith - Sunset on Mount Diablo (Marin Sunset) - Google Art Project.jpg
paintings.title: Sunset on Mount Diablo (Marin Sunset)
paintings.blurb: Scottish-born and San Francisco-raised, Keith became California's great tonalist — a close friend of John Muir, with whom he tramped the Sierra. Here the day burns down to a band of gold over the Bay Area hills, the foreground sinking into warm shadow. Keith cared less for topographic accuracy than for mood and light, and a Keith sunset feels less like a place than a feeling of evening settling over the land.
paintings.setting: Mount Diablo rises east of San Francisco Bay; its silhouette and the region's long golden sunsets were favorites of Keith's late, atmospheric style.
paintings.alt: A glowing golden sunset over rolling hills and a distant mountain, the foreground dropping into warm dusk shadow.

paintings.file: Headwaters of the San Joaquin by William Keith.jpg
paintings.title: Headwaters of the San Joaquin
paintings.blurb: High in the Sierra, where the San Joaquin River begins as snowmelt, Keith finds a wild basin of granite, water, and weathered pine. He knew this backcountry firsthand from long mountain trips, often in the company of John Muir, and the painting carries the hush of real alpine country. Warm light rakes across the rocks while the far peaks dissolve into haze — grandeur rendered with a quiet, intimate touch.
paintings.setting: The San Joaquin rises in California's high Sierra Nevada and runs down to water the Central Valley; Keith painted its rugged source country from memory and sketch.
paintings.alt: A rugged high-country basin of granite slabs and scattered pines, lit by warm light, with hazy mountain peaks beyond.

paintings.file: William Wendt - Mount San Antonio - 1913.3 - Dallas Museum of Art.jpg
paintings.title: Mount San Antonio
paintings.blurb: Often called the patriarch of Southern California landscape painting, Wendt rendered the region's hills with a reverence that bordered on the spiritual — he saw the land itself as a kind of sermon. Here Mount San Antonio, the peak locals call Old Baldy, rises above sunlit foothills built up in broad, confident strokes. Few painters captured the bones of the California landscape so plainly or so well.
paintings.setting: Mount San Antonio ('Old Baldy') is the highest summit of the San Gabriel Mountains above the Los Angeles basin, a recurring subject for Wendt.
paintings.alt: A broad mountain peak rising above green and gold foothills under a wide, bright sky.

paintings.file: Charles Marion Russell – In Without Knocking – Google Art Project.jpg
paintings.title: In Without Knocking
paintings.museum: Amon Carter Museum of American Art, Fort Worth
paintings.blurb: Russell, 'the Cowboy Artist,' had punched cattle in Montana before he ever sold a painting, and he loved telling the West's tall tales in paint. Here a band of rowdy cowhands rides right onto a saloon's porch at dusk, guns out and dust flying, in a scene half comedy and half chaos. The fading evening light, the rearing horses, the splintering rail — it's pure frontier mischief, painted by a man who'd seen plenty of it.
paintings.setting: Russell spent his life in Montana cattle country and worked from memory of the open-range era he watched fade in his own lifetime.
paintings.alt: Cowboys on horseback charging onto a wooden saloon porch at dusk, pistols firing, horses rearing amid kicked-up dust.

paintings.file: Oranges and Poppies (Boston Public Library).jpg
paintings.title: Oranges and Poppies
paintings.blurb: Louis Prang, a Boston printer, brought fine art into ordinary homes through chromolithography — color prints built up from a dozen or more inked stones, often reproducing still-lifes by leading American painters. This one gathers two California emblems in a single bowl of light: bright oranges from the state's young citrus groves and a scatter of golden poppies, the wildflower that carpets its hillsides every spring. It is a small, glowing valentine to California abundance.
paintings.setting: The California poppy is the official state flower, and the orange was the fruit that drew a generation of settlers west — both flourish across the state.
paintings.alt: A color print of a still life: ripe oranges with leaves heaped in a dish beside loose orange-gold poppies on a dark tabletop.

paintings.file: Arroyo Seco, Pasadena, by Franz Bischoff.jpg
paintings.title: Arroyo Seco, Pasadena
paintings.blurb: Bischoff trained in Austria as a porcelain decorator and arrived in America so skilled at painting flowers that he was crowned the 'King of the Rose Painters.' After settling in California he built a studio along the Arroyo Seco in South Pasadena and turned to landscape. 'I never have to go very far from home for inspiration,' he said — and the dry creek bed outside his door proved him right.
paintings.setting: The Arroyo Seco, the seasonal creek winding below Pasadena, ran right past Bischoff's studio and became his most beloved local subject.
paintings.alt: A sunlit creek bed winding between brushy banks toward distant hills under a warm sky.

paintings.file: Southern California Landscape by Maurice Braun, San Diego Museum of Art.JPG
paintings.title: Southern California Landscape
paintings.museum: San Diego Museum of Art, San Diego
paintings.blurb: Braun moved to San Diego in 1909 and found in its open hills and back country a landscape that fit his temperament exactly. A devoted student of Theosophy, he painted nature as something luminous and serene, his colors cooled into a gentle harmony. Works like this one made him a defining figure of California Impressionism in the south of the state.
paintings.setting: San Diego's rolling inland hills and valleys became Braun's lifelong subject after he settled there in 1909.
paintings.alt: Gentle rolling hills and scattered trees bathed in soft hazy light under a pale, luminous sky.

paintings.file: Edgar Alwyn Payne Alpine Lake.jpg
paintings.title: Alpine Lake
paintings.blurb: Payne was born in Missouri in 1883 and taught himself to paint while working as a house and sign painter. He spent many summers in the high Sierra with pack animals, painting outdoors for weeks at a time. Here jagged granite peaks with snowfields rise above a dark green lake, with pines and boulders along the shore.
paintings.setting: A lake below the granite peaks of the high Sierra Nevada, reached only by trail.
paintings.alt: Jagged gray granite peaks with patches of snow above a deep green mountain lake, pines and boulders on the near shore.

paintings.file: Fishing on the Merced River by Thomas Hill, 1891, oil on canvas, Saint Louis Art Museum.jpg
paintings.title: Fishing on the Merced River
paintings.blurb: Hill was born in England in 1829, came to the United States as a teenager, and moved to California in 1861. He painted Yosemite for more than forty years. Here El Capitan rises on the left and Bridalveil Fall drops on the right, while a small figure fishes from the rocks in the river below.
paintings.setting: The Merced River in Yosemite Valley, below El Capitan and Bridalveil Fall.
paintings.alt: A large granite cliff at left and a waterfall at right above a river with rocks, a small figure fishing on the bank.

paintings.file: Edgar Alwyn Payne Altadena Dawn.jpg
paintings.title: Altadena Dawn
paintings.blurb: Payne painted the foothills around Pasadena and Altadena, at the foot of the San Gabriel Mountains. In this painting the first light turns the mountain face pink and lavender while the ground below is still in shadow. A row of tall dark trees stands in front, and a little blue sky shows at the corner.
paintings.setting: Altadena, on the slopes above Pasadena, with the San Gabriel Mountains rising behind it.
paintings.alt: A large mountain glowing pink and lavender in dawn light, with a row of tall dark trees in the shaded foreground.

paintings.file: 'In the High Sierra' by Guy Rose.jpg
paintings.title: In the High Sierra
paintings.blurb: Guy Rose was born in 1867 in San Gabriel, California, the son of a rancher. After years in France he came home in 1914 and began painting the state's mountains and coast. In this tall canvas blue peaks rise above a lake that mirrors them, and dark trees line the shore.
paintings.setting: A lake in the high Sierra Nevada that reflects the peaks above it.
paintings.alt: Blue and white mountain peaks under clouds, mirrored in a still lake with a dark band of trees along the shore.

paintings.file: Mary DeNeale Morgan A Carmel Garden.jpg
paintings.title: A Carmel Garden
paintings.blurb: Morgan was born in San Francisco, studied at the California School of Design, and settled in Carmel in 1910, where she lived for the rest of her life. Here she painted a garden in bloom: tall blue delphiniums and white flowers around a stone path, a canvas umbrella over a small table, and pines behind the cottage.
paintings.setting: A cottage garden in Carmel-by-the-Sea, a town that drew painters and writers in the early 1900s.
paintings.alt: Tall blue delphiniums and white flowers around a stone path, a striped garden umbrella, a cottage and tall pines behind.

paintings.file: Edgar Alwyn Payne Bishop Pass.jpg
paintings.title: Bishop Pass
paintings.blurb: Payne often put a rider and pack animals into his Sierra paintings, and he traveled the same way himself. A man on horseback leads a pack horse along a rocky ledge, the trail's red rock in front. Behind him rise steep gray peaks streaked with snow.
paintings.setting: Bishop Pass, a high trail crossing of the Sierra crest above Bishop in the Owens Valley.
paintings.alt: A rider on a horse leading a pack horse along a red rocky ledge, steep gray mountain peaks streaked with snow behind.

paintings.file: 'Patch of Poppies' by Granville Redmond, 1912.jpg
paintings.title: Patch of Poppies
paintings.blurb: Redmond lost his hearing as a young child and studied at the California School for the Deaf in Berkeley, where his art teachers saw his talent early. In this painting a band of orange poppies and a patch of purple flowers lie across a flat field. Pink and lavender clouds fill the sky above.
paintings.setting: An open field in Southern California in spring, when poppies and other wildflowers bloom in patches.
paintings.alt: A flat field with a band of orange poppies and a patch of purple flowers, under a sky of pink and lavender clouds.

paintings.file: Jack Wilkinson Smith - 0724bc2abd.jpg
paintings.title: Sierra Autumn
paintings.blurb: Smith was born in Paterson, New Jersey, and worked as an artist-correspondent for the Cincinnati Enquirer during the Spanish-American War before moving to Southern California in 1906. There he became a founding member of the California Art Club. In this canvas, granite peaks rise above a stream, and the trees along its banks have turned yellow and red.
paintings.setting: A creek in the high Sierra Nevada in fall, below bare granite peaks.
paintings.alt: Granite mountain peaks under white clouds above a calm stream, with tall pines and trees in yellow and red along the bank.

paintings.file: Edgar Alwyn Payne California Hills.jpg
paintings.title: California Hills
paintings.blurb: Payne painted with broad, visible strokes, and he wrote later that a painter should build a picture on a few large shapes. Here the mountains are one large mass in warm orange and brown, with blue shadow in the folds. A band of dark oaks along the bottom holds the foreground.
paintings.setting: The dry mountains of Southern California in late afternoon.
paintings.alt: Large orange and brown mountains with blue shadows in their folds, a band of dark green oaks along the bottom.

paintings.file: 'Cholla near Palm Springs, California' by Franz Arthur Bischoff.jpg
paintings.title: Cholla near Palm Springs, California
paintings.blurb: Bischoff came to California in 1906 already famous as a painter of flowers on porcelain. Once settled in Pasadena he turned to landscape, and in the 1920s he traveled to the desert. Here clumps of cholla cactus stand in pale sand, with bare blue and purple mountains rising behind them.
paintings.setting: The Colorado Desert around Palm Springs, below the San Jacinto Mountains.
paintings.alt: Clumps of spiny cholla cactus in pale desert sand, with bare blue and purple mountains under a light sky.

paintings.file: Hill Thomas Mount St. Helena Napa Valley 1887.jpg
paintings.title: Mount St. Helena, Napa Valley
paintings.blurb: Hill painted many parts of California besides Yosemite. In this canvas Mount St. Helena rises at the head of the Napa Valley with snow on its slopes. A still pond in the foreground reflects the light, with bare trees and dry grass around it.
paintings.setting: Mount St. Helena, the highest peak at the north end of the Napa Valley.
paintings.alt: A broad mountain with snow on its slopes above a valley, a still pond with bare trees and dry grass in front.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne Desert Rain.jpg
paintings.title: Desert Rain
paintings.blurb: Payne painted the Southwest from the 1910s on, often traveling to Navajo country in Arizona. A storm hangs over a dark mesa, with gray streaks of rain falling at the left. Three riders cross the open ground in front, small under the clouds.
paintings.setting: The open desert of northern Arizona, where summer storms build over the mesas in the afternoon.
paintings.alt: Gray rain falling from tall clouds over a dark flat-topped mesa, three small riders on horseback crossing the desert below.

paintings.file: Huddled Houses, by William Wendt.jpg
paintings.title: Huddled Houses
paintings.blurb: William Wendt was born in Germany in 1865, came to Chicago at fifteen, and taught himself to paint. He moved to California in 1906 and became the first president of the California Art Club in 1911. Here a group of farm buildings with red roofs sits among tall eucalyptus, beside a golden field.
paintings.setting: A farmstead in Southern California, sheltered by eucalyptus planted as a windbreak.
paintings.alt: A group of farm buildings with red roofs among tall green eucalyptus trees, a golden field in front under white clouds.

paintings.file: 'Indian Tobacco Trees, La Jolla' by Guy Rose.jpg
paintings.title: Indian Tobacco Trees, La Jolla
paintings.blurb: Rose painted this on a trip to La Jolla, north of San Diego. Slender trees with pale trunks and gray-green leaves stand along a dirt path above the sea. Through them the water shows bright blue, with rocks and a white line of surf along the shore.
paintings.setting: The coast at La Jolla in San Diego County, where trails run along the bluffs above the sea.
paintings.alt: Slender trees with pale trunks along a sandy path above a bright blue sea, rocks and white surf along the shore.

paintings.file: 'Monterey Coast' by William Ritschel, after 1911.JPG
paintings.title: Monterey Coast
paintings.blurb: William Ritschel was born in Germany in 1864, worked as a sailor, and studied at the Munich Academy before coming to New York in 1895. In 1911 he moved to the Carmel Highlands and built a stone house above the sea. Here a pale sea stack stands off a cliff, with surf foaming around its base.
paintings.setting: The rocky coast south of Carmel, where Ritschel painted from his home for nearly forty years.
paintings.alt: A pale rock sea stack beside a tall cliff, green and white surf foaming around the base of the rocks.

paintings.file: Mary DeNeale Morgan Carmel Valley house.jpg
paintings.title: Carmel Valley
paintings.blurb: Morgan worked often in gouache, a water-based paint that dries flat and opaque, and this small picture is painted on illustration board. A pair of slim trees with orange leaves stands before a white farmhouse, and a creek winds through the dry grass. Blue mountains rise behind under a gray sky.
paintings.setting: Carmel Valley, which runs inland from the coast at Carmel along the Carmel River.
paintings.alt: Slim trees with orange autumn leaves beside a white farmhouse and a winding creek, blue mountains under a gray sky.

paintings.file: Indian Canoes near Muir Glacier, oil on canvas painting by Thomas Hill, c. 1910, Anchorage Museum.jpg
paintings.title: Indian Canoes near Muir Glacier
paintings.blurb: Hill traveled to Alaska late in the 1880s and painted Glacier Bay and its ice for years afterward. In this canvas pink and gray clouds wrap a sharp peak, and the water below is calm and pale. A canoe with several paddlers crosses the bay near the shore.
paintings.setting: Glacier Bay in southeast Alaska, where Muir Glacier, named for John Muir, once met the sea.
paintings.alt: Pink and gray clouds wrapped around a sharp mountain peak above a calm pale bay, with a canoe of paddlers near the shore.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne Edgar Payne Canyon Mission Viejo, Capistrano.jpg
paintings.title: Canyon Mission Viejo, Capistrano
paintings.blurb: Payne moved to Laguna Beach in 1917 and painted the hills and canyons behind it, which were then cattle range. In this view late sun lights a stand of oaks in gold while the mountain behind turns lavender. The sky above is a pale, warm yellow.
paintings.setting: The canyons of Rancho Mission Viejo in southern Orange County, inland from San Juan Capistrano.
paintings.alt: A lavender mountain under a pale yellow sky, with dark oaks and golden sunlit trees in a valley below.

paintings.file: Carl Oscar Borg A Summer Day, Pacific Coast.jpg
paintings.title: A Summer Day, Pacific Coast
paintings.blurb: Before he became known for the Southwest, Borg painted the California coast around Los Angeles and Santa Barbara, where he lived for much of his career. A broad oak takes the right side of this canvas, and a few thin trees lean in the wind on the left. Between them the grass runs down to rocks and a band of blue sea under a summer sky.
paintings.setting: The bluffs above the Pacific in Southern California, where coast live oaks grow close to the shore.
paintings.alt: A large dark oak and a few slender trees on a grassy bluff with scattered rocks, the blue ocean and white clouds beyond.

paintings.file: California Poppies and Eucalyptus, by Granville Redmond.jpg
paintings.title: California Poppies and Eucalyptus
paintings.blurb: Redmond's poppy paintings sold well, and he made many of them in the 1910s and 1920s. Here a slope is covered with orange poppies mixed with blue lupine. Tall eucalyptus trees stand on the hill, and a bright blue mountain rises behind them.
paintings.setting: A hillside in Southern California in spring, with eucalyptus planted along its top.
paintings.alt: A slope covered with orange poppies and blue lupine, tall eucalyptus trees on the hill and a blue mountain behind.

paintings.file: Guy Rose - Carmel Hills.jpg
paintings.title: Carmel Hills
paintings.blurb: Rose spent summers painting on the Monterey Peninsula after he came back from France. In this canvas a sandy track and a rail fence lead into a green valley with clumps of cypress. Bare tan hills rise behind it, and blue mountains sit under gray clouds on the horizon.
paintings.setting: The hills behind Carmel-by-the-Sea, where dunes give way to pasture and cypress groves.
paintings.alt: A sandy track and rail fence leading into a green valley with cypress trees, tan hills and blue mountains under gray clouds.

paintings.file: An Autumnal Sunset on the Russian River Evening Glow by William Keith, 1878.jpg
paintings.title: An Autumnal Sunset on the Russian River (Evening Glow)
paintings.museum: Butler Institute of American Art, Youngstown, Ohio
paintings.blurb: The sky does most of the work in this painting. Clouds of orange and red streak across a blue sky above a valley in shadow. Dark pines stand along the left, and the river valley opens in the middle distance.
paintings.setting: The Russian River valley in Sonoma County, in autumn.
paintings.alt: Clouds lit orange and red across a blue sky above a shadowed valley, dark pines along the left side.

paintings.file: Mary DeNeale Morgan Carmel Valley Ranch.jpg
paintings.title: Carmel Valley Ranch
paintings.blurb: Morgan painted the farms of Carmel Valley as often as the coast. In this square canvas a white farmhouse with a steep gable sits among trees, with a red-roofed building beside it. A figure walks along a fence in the dry grass, and the hills behind are patched with gold and blue.
paintings.setting: A ranch in Carmel Valley, where farms and orchards lined the river before the area was built up.
paintings.alt: A white farmhouse with a steep roof and a red-roofed building among trees, a fence and figure in the foreground, gold hills behind.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne Edgar Payne Capistrano Canyon.jpg
paintings.title: Capistrano Canyon
paintings.blurb: This is one of Payne's softer paintings, close in mood to the work of his Laguna neighbors. A sycamore with yellowing leaves stands at the left, and a sunny meadow opens in front. The hills behind are painted in pale violet and white, as if seen through a light haze.
paintings.setting: A canyon in the hills near San Juan Capistrano, in southern Orange County.
paintings.alt: A tall sycamore with yellow leaves beside a sunny meadow, small trees beyond and pale violet hills in a light haze.

paintings.file: Jack Wilkinson Smith - 08d494382a.jpg
paintings.title: California Landscape
paintings.blurb: Smith painted both the mountains and the sea, and he often let the weather set the mood. Here the ridges have gone dark blue under heavy clouds, while a patch of clear sky opens above them. The valley floor below is in shadow, with only a few lighter strokes for water and brush.
paintings.setting: A mountain valley in Southern California under a passing storm.
paintings.alt: Dark blue mountain ridges under heavy white and gray clouds, a patch of blue sky, and a shadowed valley floor below.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne Edgar Payne Edgar Payne A Rider with Packhorses in the Sierra.jpg
paintings.title: A Rider with Packhorses in the Sierra
paintings.blurb: Payne and his wife, the painter Elsie Palmer Payne, spent summers camping in the Sierra with pack animals carrying their paints and canvases. In this painting a rider leads a loaded horse across a green slope among boulders. Gray peaks with snow in their gullies fill the view behind.
paintings.setting: The High Sierra above the Owens Valley, where Payne painted almost every summer.
paintings.alt: A rider on horseback with a loaded pack horse on a green slope among boulders, gray mountains with snowy gullies behind.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne Eucalypti.jpg
paintings.title: Eucalypti
paintings.blurb: Eucalyptus trees came to California from Australia in the 1800s and were planted by the thousands for timber and windbreaks. The painters of Southern California made them a regular subject. Here tall, loose trees stand across a grassy field, their trunks pale and their crowns dark against white clouds.
paintings.setting: A field of eucalyptus in Southern California, where the trees were planted along roads and ranch edges.
paintings.alt: Tall eucalyptus trees with pale trunks and dark green crowns spread across a grassy field under white clouds.

paintings.file: Crashing Waves in a Rocky Coastal View by Franz A. Bischoff.jpg
paintings.title: Crashing Waves in a Rocky Coastal View
paintings.blurb: Bischoff built this coastal scene out of broad, flat strokes of color, laid side by side with little blending. Gray rocks step down to the water, white surf breaks against them, and green and orange slopes rise above. It is a small oil on canvasboard, likely painted outdoors in one sitting.
paintings.setting: A rocky stretch of the California coast, where Bischoff often painted on trips from his Pasadena home.
paintings.alt: Gray rocks stepping down to white surf, with green and orange slopes and dark trees rising above the shore.

paintings.file: Lake at Yosemite, California by Thomas Hill.jpg
paintings.title: Lake at Yosemite, California
paintings.blurb: This small oil on board shows a quieter side of Hill's Yosemite. A pink granite cliff rises above a still lake in warm light. A tight group of tall pines stands on the right bank, and the near shore is dry grass.
paintings.setting: A lake in the Yosemite region, under granite cliffs warmed by late sun.
paintings.alt: A pink granite cliff above a still lake in warm light, a group of tall pines on the right bank and dry grass in front.

paintings.file: Guy Rose - Early Morning (c. 1905-1912).jpg
paintings.title: Early Morning
paintings.blurb: From 1904 to 1912 Rose lived in Giverny, the French village where Claude Monet had his garden, and he painted its fields in all seasons. Here two tall poplars catch the early light, their leaves yellow-green. A row of pollarded willows crosses the bright meadow, and a wooded hill rises behind.
paintings.setting: The meadows along the Epte River at Giverny, in Normandy, where many American painters lived around Monet.
paintings.alt: Two tall poplar trees in yellow-green leaf over a bright green meadow, a row of willows and a wooded hill behind.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne Eucalyptus Landscape, California.jpg
paintings.title: Eucalyptus Landscape, California
paintings.blurb: Payne painted this grove from close in, so the trunks rise past the top of the canvas. Through the gaps a cluster of white and red-roofed buildings sits in a clearing. He kept the colors cool, with blue-green leaves and gray-brown bark.
paintings.setting: A eucalyptus grove beside a small settlement in Southern California.
paintings.alt: Tall eucalyptus trunks and blue-green leaves in the foreground, with white buildings and red roofs visible through the trees.

paintings.file: Mary DeNeale Morgan Carmel Valley.jpg
paintings.title: Carmel Valley
paintings.blurb: In this oil on masonite Morgan simplified the mountains into large shapes of color. The near ridges are red and purple, the far ones blue, and the flat floor of the valley is pale gold. White clouds sit along the highest peaks.
paintings.setting: The Santa Lucia Range above Carmel Valley, seen across the flat valley floor.
paintings.alt: Mountain ridges in red, purple and blue rising above a flat, pale valley floor, with white clouds along the peaks.

paintings.file: Carl Oscar Borg California Landscape.jpg
paintings.title: California Landscape
paintings.blurb: Borg taught himself much of his craft while working as a house and ship painter, and he kept a plain, solid way of building a scene. One dark tree stands on a green rise, a creek bed of white stones runs below it, and the sea shows at the far left. A gray sky presses down on everything, the kind of weather that comes in off the Pacific in late winter.
paintings.setting: A coastal valley in California after rain, when the hills turn green and the creeks run again.
paintings.alt: A dark, rounded tree on a green hillside above a stream of white rocks, the sea at left under a heavy gray sky.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne Eucalyptus Trees.jpg
paintings.title: Eucalyptus Trees
paintings.blurb: In this painting two tall eucalyptus trees stand close together on the left, with a single thinner one on the right. Gray-green sage covers the ground in front. Payne used short, separate strokes for the leaves and left the sky a bright mix of white cloud and blue.
paintings.setting: Open land in Southern California with sage scrub and planted eucalyptus.
paintings.alt: Tall dark eucalyptus trees on either side of a field of gray-green sage, white clouds and blue sky behind.

paintings.file: Frank Cuprien - 591421285a.jpg
paintings.title: Golden Sunset, Laguna Beach
paintings.blurb: Cuprien painted the sea at Laguna Beach so often that the town came to call him its dean of painters. He liked the hour when the light goes soft and the color of the water changes by the minute. In this canvas long waves roll in under a sky of pink and gray, and a pale band of light lies across the water near the horizon.
paintings.setting: The open Pacific off Laguna Beach in Orange County, which Cuprien watched and painted for most of his life.
paintings.alt: Long gray-green waves rolling toward the viewer under a pale sky of pink and gray clouds, with light on the far water.

paintings.file: Saddleback Mountain, by William Wendt.jpg
paintings.title: Saddleback Mountain
paintings.blurb: Wendt settled in Laguna Beach and painted the Santa Ana Mountains behind it many times. In this tall canvas sycamores with white trunks and orange leaves frame the double summit of Saddleback, painted in violet and blue. A dry riverbed runs across the middle.
paintings.setting: Saddleback, the two peaks of Santiago and Modjeska in the Santa Ana Mountains, seen from much of Orange County.
paintings.alt: White-trunked sycamores with orange leaves framing a violet two-peaked mountain, a dry riverbed across the middle.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne High Sierra Landscape, Big Pine Canyon.jpg
paintings.title: High Sierra Landscape, Big Pine Canyon
paintings.blurb: Big Pine Canyon was one of Payne's favorite places in the Sierra. In this canvas a stream runs over rocks in the foreground, green shrubs and pines grow along it, and a wall of pale peaks with snow in their chutes rises behind. He painted the rock in warm pinks and violets.
paintings.setting: Big Pine Canyon, west of the town of Big Pine, which leads up to the Palisade Glacier, the largest in the Sierra Nevada.
paintings.alt: A rocky stream with green shrubs and pines in front of pale pink and violet peaks with snow in their gullies.

paintings.file: Granville Redmond - A Field of California Poppies.jpg
paintings.title: A Field of California Poppies
paintings.blurb: Redmond often put the poppies in a narrow band and gave most of the canvas to the sky, as he did here. A strip of orange flowers runs across a flat green field. Above it large white and gray clouds stack up against blue.
paintings.setting: The open coastal plain of Southern California in spring.
paintings.alt: A narrow band of orange poppies across a flat green field, with large white and gray clouds filling the sky above.

paintings.file: N10151-47-web.jpg
paintings.title: Yosemite Valley
paintings.blurb: Hill signed and dated this large canvas in 1880, the year he was painting Yosemite most intensely. El Capitan rises at the left and Bridalveil Fall drops on the right. Small figures rest by a camp on the valley floor, in warm afternoon light.
paintings.setting: The floor of Yosemite Valley, looking east between El Capitan and Bridalveil Fall.
paintings.alt: A tall pale granite cliff at left and a waterfall on the right cliff, with small figures resting on the sunlit valley floor.

paintings.file: Berkeley Oaks by William Keith.jpg
paintings.title: Berkeley Oaks
paintings.blurb: Keith lived in Berkeley and painted its oaks in his later years. In this canvas old oaks frame a pond in a clearing, and a white cloud lights up the sky beyond. A small figure stands near the water, and the shade under the trees is warm brown.
paintings.setting: The oak woodland of Berkeley, on the east side of San Francisco Bay.
paintings.alt: Old oak trees framing a pond in a clearing, a bright white cloud in a blue-green sky and a small figure by the water.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne High Sierra, Mountain Scene.jpg
paintings.title: High Sierra, Mountain Scene
paintings.blurb: Payne's Sierra paintings often follow the same plan: dark trees and rocks close by, a lake in the middle, a peak above. Here a broad mountain with snowfields rises over a blue lake. Dark pines and a red-brown snag stand on the boulders in front.
paintings.setting: A lake basin above timberline in the high Sierra Nevada.
paintings.alt: A broad gray mountain with white snowfields above a blue lake, dark pines and a red-brown dead tree on boulders in front.

paintings.file: 'Brown Hills on the Russian River' by Benjamin Chambers Brown, 1914.jpg
paintings.title: Brown Hills on the Russian River
paintings.blurb: Brown came to Pasadena from Arkansas in 1896 and stayed for the rest of his life, painting the hills and arroyos around him and later making etchings with his brother Howell. This small oil on panel, under nine inches wide, comes from a trip north. He gave most of the surface to the bare summer hills, their grass already dry, with a weathered shed and a few dark trees to set the scale.
paintings.setting: The Russian River runs through Sonoma County to the Pacific, past oak woodland and grassy hills that turn tan by early summer.
paintings.alt: Tan, bare hills rolling toward blue ridges, with clumps of green trees and a small weathered wooden shed in a golden field.

paintings.file: Jack Wilkinson Smith - 1ce43dea5e.jpg
paintings.title: Solitude
paintings.blurb: Smith returned to the forests of the Sierra many times. In this painting he stood among tall pines and looked toward a sunlit clearing, with a dead snag standing pale among the living trees. The light falls in patches on the forest floor, and no person appears anywhere in the scene.
paintings.setting: A pine forest in the Sierra Nevada, where Smith painted on long summer trips.
paintings.alt: Tall pine trees around a sunlit forest clearing, a pale dead tree trunk standing among them, light falling in patches on the ground.

paintings.file: 'Foothills' by Maurice Braun, 1934.jpg
paintings.title: Foothills
paintings.blurb: Braun was born in Hungary, grew up in New York, and studied with William Merritt Chase before moving to San Diego in 1909. He opened an art school there and painted the back country for the rest of his life. In this view a valley of green fields lies below a hillside of eucalyptus and brush, with blue mountains on the horizon.
paintings.setting: The foothills east of San Diego, where farms and ranches filled the valleys in the 1930s.
paintings.alt: A valley of green fields below a brushy hillside with eucalyptus trees, blue mountains on the horizon under a pale sky.

paintings.file: Guy Rose - July Afternoon (c. 1907-1912).jpg
paintings.title: July Afternoon
paintings.blurb: Rose painted this in Giverny in high summer, with a soft haze over everything. A haystack stands in a green field behind a low hedge, and a broken wooden fence leans at the center. Round trees fill the far edge of the field under a pale sky.
paintings.setting: Farm fields at Giverny in Normandy, the village where Rose lived among other American painters for eight years.
paintings.alt: A haystack in a green field behind a low hedge and a broken wooden fence, round trees and a pale hazy sky behind.

paintings.file: Monterey Coast- 17 Mile Drive LACMA M.91.144.jpg
paintings.title: Monterey Coast, 17 Mile Drive
paintings.museum: Los Angeles County Museum of Art
paintings.blurb: Theodore Wores was born in San Francisco in 1859, studied in Munich, and spent several years painting in Japan in the 1880s and 1890s. Later he worked along the California coast. Here pale dunes with small flowers lead down to a turquoise sea, with low rocks offshore.
paintings.setting: 17-Mile Drive, the coastal road around the Monterey Peninsula through Pebble Beach.
paintings.alt: Pale sand dunes dotted with small flowers and green shrubs sloping to a turquoise sea with low rocks offshore.

paintings.file: Carmel Valley Pasture Land.jpg
paintings.title: Carmel Valley Pasture Land
paintings.blurb: Ritschel is known for the sea, but here he turned inland. Cattle graze in a green pasture between dark cypress trees, and a stretch of water shows beyond. Large clouds fill the sky, painted with the same broad strokes he used for surf.
paintings.setting: Pasture land near the mouth of Carmel Valley, close to the coast.
paintings.alt: Cattle grazing in a green pasture between dark cypress trees, water beyond and large white clouds filling the sky.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne High Sierras.jpg
paintings.title: High Sierras
paintings.blurb: This painting is almost all mountain. A single peak in gray and violet fills the frame, with patches of snow on its ledges. At its base a small lake shows dark blue-green, and a few pines stand at the left edge.
paintings.setting: A cirque in the high Sierra Nevada, where a lake sits at the foot of a steep peak.
paintings.alt: A massive gray and violet mountain peak with patches of snow, a small dark lake at its base and a few pines at left.

paintings.file: Mary DeNeale Morgan Cypress at Monterey.jpg
paintings.title: Cypress at Monterey
paintings.blurb: The Monterey cypress grows wild in only two places, both on the Monterey Peninsula, and Morgan painted these trees for decades. In this gouache, tall bare trunks lean in the wind, their dark crowns flattened at the top. The sea and a strip of white sand show between them, with orange grass in front.
paintings.setting: The Monterey Peninsula, one of two places in the world where the Monterey cypress grows naturally.
paintings.alt: Tall, leaning cypress trunks with dark flattened crowns above orange grass, the sea and white sand visible between them.

paintings.file: Painting of Wawona Hotel by Thomas Hill.jpeg
paintings.title: Wawona Hotel
paintings.blurb: Hill's daughter married into the Washburn family, who ran the Wawona Hotel, and from the 1880s Hill kept a studio beside it. He painted the hotel here as a long white building with a deep porch, set in a meadow below the pines. A stagecoach pulls up in front, bringing visitors to the park.
paintings.setting: Wawona, in the southern part of Yosemite National Park, where Hill's studio still stands beside the hotel.
paintings.alt: A long white two-story hotel with a porch in a green meadow, tall pines and mountains behind and a stagecoach in front.

paintings.file: California Oaks and Field by William Keith.jpg
paintings.title: California Oaks and Field
paintings.blurb: This is one of Keith's dark, late paintings, where most of the canvas sits in shadow. Heavy oaks crowd the frame, and light falls on a single patch of grass in the clearing between them. Keith wanted these pictures to give a mood more than a record of a place.
paintings.setting: An oak grove in Northern California in late afternoon light.
paintings.alt: Heavy dark oak trees crowding the frame, with light falling on a single patch of grass in a clearing.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne High Surf along the Laguna Coast.jpg
paintings.title: High Surf along the Laguna Coast
paintings.blurb: Payne helped found the Laguna Beach Art Association in 1918 and served as its first president. He painted the coast there in all conditions. In this canvas a wave explodes against dark rocks, white foam covering the green water. A low headland runs out along the horizon.
paintings.setting: The rocky coves of Laguna Beach, where winter swells break hard against the reefs.
paintings.alt: A large wave breaking into white foam against dark rocks, green water around them and a low headland on the horizon.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne Hills of the Southland.jpg
paintings.title: Hills of the Southland
paintings.blurb: Southland is an old name for Southern California, used in the region's newspapers and promotions in Payne's time. He painted the mountains here in cool gray and violet, ridge behind ridge. In front lies a green valley with dark trees and a field of light.
paintings.setting: A valley below the mountains of Southern California, painted when much of the land was still open.
paintings.alt: Gray-violet mountain ridges under white clouds above a green valley with dark trees and a sunlit field.

paintings.file: Carl Oscar Borg Indian Encampment.jpg
paintings.title: Indian Encampment
paintings.blurb: Borg spent long stretches in Navajo and Hopi country from the 1910s through the 1930s, and he worked as an art director in Hollywood between trips. In this camp a covered wagon stands with its horses at the foot of a dark hill while people gather near a fire. Storm clouds roll over the scene, and a patch of clear turquoise sky opens behind them.
paintings.setting: A camp on the high desert of the Southwest, with a wagon, horses, and a fire at the end of the day.
paintings.alt: A covered wagon, horses, and people around a small fire below a dark hill, gray storm clouds and a patch of turquoise sky above.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne Indians Riding through the Canyon de Chelly.jpg
paintings.title: Indians Riding through the Canyon de Chelly
paintings.blurb: Payne first went to Canyon de Chelly in the 1910s and returned for many years. A sheer sandstone wall rises on the right in bright sun, and the far walls are in blue shadow. Three Navajo riders cross the sandy floor, small at the bottom of the frame.
paintings.setting: Canyon de Chelly, on the Navajo Nation in Arizona, where Navajo families still live and farm on the canyon floor.
paintings.alt: A tall sunlit sandstone wall at right and shaded canyon walls at left, three riders crossing the sandy canyon floor.

paintings.file: Guy Rose - Laguna Eucalyptus.jpg
paintings.title: Laguna Eucalyptus
paintings.blurb: Rose painted this tall canvas in his first years back in California. A grove of eucalyptus leans along a ridge, the thin pale trunks bending and the dark crowns spread like umbrellas. White clouds pile up in the blue sky behind them.
paintings.setting: The hills above Laguna Beach, where eucalyptus had been planted along the ridges.
paintings.alt: A grove of tall eucalyptus trees with thin pale trunks and dark rounded crowns, leaning along a ridge under white clouds.

paintings.file: Franz A. Bischoff - Zion Park.jpg
paintings.title: Zion Park
paintings.blurb: In his later years Bischoff traveled beyond California to the canyons of Utah and Arizona. In Zion he painted the sandstone peaks in strong color: the tops lit orange and gold, the faces in red and violet shadow, and green trees on the slopes below. A patch of clear blue sky sits above them.
paintings.setting: Zion Canyon in southern Utah, made a national park in 1919.
paintings.alt: Towering red and orange sandstone peaks lit by sun, blue shadows on their faces, and green trees on the slopes below.

paintings.file: Resting By A Stream.jpg
paintings.title: Resting by a Stream
paintings.blurb: Hill painted this in 1866, early in his long work in the Sierra. Granite cliffs rise on both sides, with a pale spire at the right. A stream winds through the valley floor, and a few small figures rest among the rocks and trees on its bank.
paintings.setting: A granite valley in the Sierra Nevada, painted in the years when Yosemite was first set aside for public use.
paintings.alt: Granite cliffs and a pale rock spire above a winding stream and dark trees, small figures resting on the bank.

paintings.file: California Pines by William Keith, LACMA 29.19 (1 of 2).jpg
paintings.title: California Pines
paintings.museum: Los Angeles County Museum of Art
paintings.blurb: Keith often walked the Sierra with his friend John Muir in the 1870s. In this painting a snowy peak breaks out of the clouds above a valley, and dark pines stand on the slopes on both sides. A small stream runs through the valley floor.
paintings.setting: A valley in the Sierra Nevada, of the kind Keith and Muir explored together.
paintings.alt: A snowy peak emerging from clouds above a green valley, dark pines on the slopes on both sides and a small stream below.

paintings.file: Granville Redmond - After the Rain.jpg
paintings.title: After the Rain
paintings.blurb: Before the poppies, Redmond was known for quiet scenes in muted color, and this is one of them. A dirt road with puddles runs between dark trees toward the horizon. The clouds are breaking up after a storm, and a little blue sky shows through.
paintings.setting: A country road in Southern California just after a winter rain.
paintings.alt: A wet dirt road with puddles running between dark trees, gray clouds breaking up to show patches of blue sky.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne Laguna Beach Coast.jpg
paintings.title: Laguna Beach Coast
paintings.blurb: In this painting the late sun strikes the cliffs and turns them bright orange and gold, while the water below is a deep, dark blue. Payne painted the hills above the cliffs in purple. The contrast between the warm land and the cold sea carries the whole picture.
paintings.setting: The bluffs of Laguna Beach in late afternoon, when the sun sits low over the ocean.
paintings.alt: Bright orange and gold sunlit cliffs above deep dark-blue water, with purple hills along the top under a pale sky.

paintings.file: Mary DeNeale Morgan Cypress Trees Carmel.jpg
paintings.title: Cypress Trees, Carmel
paintings.blurb: This large canvas is one of Morgan's brighter paintings. Pale cypress trunks frame a view of the sea, which she painted a strong turquoise with white surf. The crowns of the trees reach across the top of the picture, and a path runs down toward the water.
paintings.setting: The shore near Carmel, where cypress groves grow right to the edge of the sea.
paintings.alt: Pale cypress trunks framing a view of a turquoise sea with white surf, a path and rocks in the foreground.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne Lake in the High Sierras.jpg
paintings.title: Lake in the High Sierras
paintings.blurb: Jagged granite spires with snowfields fill the top of this canvas, lit white and pale blue. Below them a dark band of forest runs down to a lake in deep shadow. Payne often set the bright peaks against a dark foreground this way, so the light seems to sit only on the high rock.
paintings.setting: A lake below the jagged crest of the High Sierra, reached by trail from the Owens Valley.
paintings.alt: Jagged white granite peaks with snowfields above a dark forest and a shadowed mountain lake.

paintings.file: Royal Arches And Half Dome Yosemite.jpg
paintings.title: Royal Arches and Half Dome, Yosemite
paintings.blurb: The curved bands of rock on the left are the Royal Arches, carved by the peeling of the granite in layers. Half Dome stands pale in the center, and snow lies on the peaks behind it. The Merced River runs quietly across the front, past dark pines.
paintings.setting: The east end of Yosemite Valley, where the Royal Arches face Half Dome across the Merced River.
paintings.alt: Curved bands of pale rock at left and the sheer face of Half Dome in the center, dark pines and a calm river in front.

paintings.file: California Ranch by William Keith, 1908.jpg
paintings.title: California Ranch
paintings.museum: Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco (de Young)
paintings.blurb: Keith painted this two years after the 1906 earthquake and fire, which destroyed about two thousand of his works in his San Francisco studio. Large oaks with spreading limbs frame the view, and a road runs past them across dry ground. A pale blue sky shows between the trees.
paintings.setting: Ranch land in the oak country of Northern California.
paintings.alt: Large oak trees with long spreading limbs framing a view of dry ranch land, a road running past under a pale sky.

paintings.file: Frank Cuprien - 67246f5a87.jpg
paintings.title: Seascape
paintings.blurb: Most of Cuprien's paintings show open water, but in this one he framed the sea with the land. A twisted tree leans out from a rocky point, its branches hanging over clear blue-green water. Across the cove a sunlit headland closes the view, and small rocks break the surface near the shore.
paintings.setting: A rocky cove on the Southern California coast, where trees grow to the edge of the cliffs.
paintings.alt: A leaning tree reaches out over clear turquoise water from a rocky cliff, with a sunlit headland across the cove.

paintings.file: Valley Landscape by William Wendt.jpg
paintings.title: Valley Landscape
paintings.blurb: This small study on board is under six inches tall. Wendt painted it quickly, with thick strokes: a green valley with round trees, a few red-roofed houses, and blue mountains behind under a gray sky.
paintings.setting: A farming valley in Southern California in the green season.
paintings.alt: A small study of a green valley with round trees and a few red-roofed houses, blue mountains and a gray sky behind.

paintings.file: Guy Rose - Laguna Trees (c. 1916).jpg
paintings.title: Laguna Trees
paintings.blurb: In this painting wind-bent eucalyptus trees stand on a sunny slope above the sea. Rose painted the leaves in light green and the sky in quick strokes of white and blue. The water shows only as a pale strip at the left edge.
paintings.setting: The coastal hills of Laguna Beach, where a steady sea breeze shapes the trees.
paintings.alt: Wind-bent eucalyptus trees with light green leaves on a sunny slope, the sea a pale strip at left under white clouds.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne Packing Out from Payne Lake.jpg
paintings.title: Packing Out from Payne Lake
paintings.blurb: The title names Payne Lake, a lake in the Sierra that carries the painter's name. In this canvas a rider and his pack animals start down a green slope dotted with rocks. Gray peaks with snow patches fill the background, and white clouds sit along the ridgeline.
paintings.setting: The high country of the Sierra Nevada, where Payne spent his summers painting outdoors.
paintings.alt: A rider leading pack animals down a green, rocky slope, with gray snow-patched mountains and white clouds behind.

paintings.file: Colin Campbell Cooper - Palace of Fine Arts, San Francisco.jpg
paintings.title: Palace of Fine Arts, San Francisco
paintings.blurb: Cooper traveled to San Francisco in 1915 to paint the Panama-Pacific International Exposition. He painted the Palace of Fine Arts at night, its domed rotunda lit gold against a dark blue sky. The colonnades and the dome reflect in the lagoon in front, and dark trees fill the foreground.
paintings.setting: The Palace of Fine Arts, built for the 1915 exposition and the only one of its main buildings still standing in San Francisco.
paintings.alt: A domed rotunda and curving colonnades glowing gold at night, reflected in a dark lagoon beneath a deep blue sky.

paintings.file: Mary DeNeale Morgan Cypress trees.jpg
paintings.title: Cypress Trees
paintings.blurb: This is a small oil on board, eight by ten inches, likely painted outdoors. One cypress fills the center, its pale trunk twisting and its green branches swept sideways by the wind. Morgan painted the sea behind it in quick blue and white strokes.
paintings.setting: The windy coast of the Monterey Peninsula, where steady sea winds shape the cypress trees.
paintings.alt: A single twisted cypress tree with a pale trunk and wind-swept green branches, a blue sea with white surf behind it.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne Poplars.jpg
paintings.title: Poplars
paintings.blurb: Payne simplified these three poplars into tall, flame-shaped masses of yellow and olive, lit from one side. The ground is orange and the sky behind them blue with warm clouds. In his 1941 book, Composition of Outdoor Painting, he argued that a few strong shapes matter more than detail, and this canvas shows that idea at work.
paintings.setting: A row of poplars in autumn, the kind planted along farm roads and ditches in the West.
paintings.alt: Three tall poplar trees in yellow and olive leaf standing in an orange field under a blue sky with warm clouds.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne Riders in Canyon de Chelly.jpg
paintings.title: Riders in Canyon de Chelly
paintings.blurb: In this painting the near cliff is red in full sun and the far walls are blue and violet in shade. Three riders on horseback cross the pale, flat floor of the canyon between them. A few white clouds float in a bright blue sky.
paintings.setting: Canyon de Chelly, protected as a national monument since 1931, on land the Navajo Nation still owns and farms.
paintings.alt: A towering red sunlit cliff at left and blue-violet shaded canyon walls at right, three small riders crossing the pale canyon floor.

paintings.file: Granville Redmond - Blue flowers.jpg
paintings.title: Blue Flowers
paintings.blurb: This painting is mostly blue and purple: a hillside of lupine running in drifts toward a line of blue hills. Yellow flowers fill the spaces between the drifts. Redmond painted it with short, broken strokes so the colors mix in the eye.
paintings.setting: A hillside in Southern California covered with lupine in spring.
paintings.alt: A hillside covered in drifts of blue and purple lupine with yellow flowers between, low blue hills behind.

paintings.file: Guy Rose - San Gabriel road.jpg
paintings.title: San Gabriel Road
paintings.blurb: Rose grew up in the San Gabriel Valley on his family's ranch, so this was home ground. A shaded lane runs between low whitewashed buildings and a wooden fence, under pepper trees. Light falls through the leaves in patches on the dirt, and a bench sits against the wall.
paintings.setting: An old road in San Gabriel, near the Spanish mission founded there in 1771.
paintings.alt: A shaded dirt lane between low white buildings and a wooden fence, pepper trees overhead and patches of sunlight on the ground.

paintings.file: Rock Coast at Carmel Highlands.png
paintings.title: Rock Coast at Carmel Highlands
paintings.blurb: This oil on board shows the coast right below Ritschel's home. Brown rocks step down into white, churning surf, and cypress trees lean from the cliffs above. A light fog softens the far headland.
paintings.setting: The Carmel Highlands, south of Carmel, where the Santa Lucia Mountains drop to the sea.
paintings.alt: Brown rocks stepping down into white churning surf, cypress trees leaning from the cliffs, and fog on the far headland.

paintings.file: Franz Bischoff - Aroyo Seco Bridge 1912.jpg
paintings.title: Arroyo Seco Bridge
paintings.blurb: Bischoff built his home and studio on the edge of the Arroyo Seco in South Pasadena, so the canyon was close at hand. In this painting a white concrete bridge with arched spans crosses the dry, stony riverbed. Brush and tall trees line the banks, and blue mountains stand behind under a sky of white clouds.
paintings.setting: The Arroyo Seco, a canyon that runs from the San Gabriel Mountains through Pasadena to the Los Angeles River.
paintings.alt: A white concrete bridge with arches spans a dry, rocky riverbed, with brush, tall trees and blue mountains behind.

paintings.file: Thomas Hill - Emerald Lake Near Tahoe 1890-1900.jpg
paintings.title: Emerald Lake near Tahoe
paintings.blurb: Hill painted Lake Tahoe from the 1860s on, returning to it in his late years. Here the evening sun turns a mountain slope orange above a calm lake. Dark trees stand on the left shore, and a few figures sit at the water's edge.
paintings.setting: The basin of Lake Tahoe in the Sierra Nevada, on the California and Nevada line.
paintings.alt: A mountain slope lit orange by evening sun above a calm lake, dark trees on the left shore and small figures at the edge.

paintings.file: Mary DeNeale Morgan Desert Palms.jpg
paintings.title: Desert Palms
paintings.blurb: Morgan is known for the Monterey coast, but she also painted the desert. Here tall palms stand along the edge of white sand, their trunks casting long blue shadows across it. A ridge of purple mountains closes the view behind them.
paintings.setting: The Colorado Desert of Southern California, where palm groves grow along springs and faults.
paintings.alt: Tall palm trees on white desert sand with long blue shadows, a ridge of purple mountains behind them.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne Santa Cruz Island.jpg
paintings.title: Santa Cruz Island
paintings.blurb: Payne painted the Channel Islands off the Southern California coast on boat trips from the mainland. Here the evening sun lights a headland bright orange, while the water in front has gone dark. A dark rock at the lower right frames the view.
paintings.setting: Santa Cruz Island, the largest of the Channel Islands, now part of Channel Islands National Park.
paintings.alt: A headland lit bright orange by low sun above dark, rippled water, with a dark rock in the lower right corner.

paintings.file: Jack Wilkinson Smith - 4cc458f914.jpg
paintings.title: Cabin in the Sierras
paintings.blurb: Smith often painted the Sierra from the ground a hiker would stand on, with a trail or a fence to lead the eye in. Here a small wooden cabin sits in a dry meadow behind a split-rail fence, a band of green pines behind it. Two bare peaks rise above the trees, and white clouds drift across the sky.
paintings.setting: A meadow in the high Sierra Nevada, with a cabin built at the edge of the forest.
paintings.alt: A small wooden cabin behind a rail fence in a dry meadow, green pines behind it and two bare mountain peaks above.

paintings.file: Carl Oscar Borg The Red Rock Wall.jpg
paintings.title: The Red Rock Wall
paintings.blurb: The sandstone canyons of Arizona gave Borg his largest subjects. In this painting a sheer wall of pale rock fills almost the whole canvas, its face streaked by water. Below it a rider in a red shirt crosses a shallow stream on horseback, small against the cliff, with a few green trees along the bank.
paintings.setting: A sandstone canyon in the Southwest, where streams cut deep walls through the plateau.
paintings.alt: A tall wall of pale, streaked sandstone towering over a shallow stream, with a lone rider on horseback and a few green trees.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne Shadow Slope, Inyo County, California, near Bishop.jpg
paintings.title: Shadow Slope, Inyo County, California, near Bishop
paintings.blurb: The title points to the shadow that covers most of this canvas. The late sun lights only the top of a jagged ridge in gold and pink, while the slope below is already dark green and gray. Boulders and a small lake sit in the shaded basin at the bottom.
paintings.setting: The east side of the Sierra Nevada near Bishop, in Inyo County, where the mountains rise steeply from the Owens Valley.
paintings.alt: A jagged ridge lit gold and pink at the top, with a dark shaded slope, boulders and a small lake below.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne Sierra Divide.jpg
paintings.title: Sierra Divide
paintings.blurb: Payne painted snow on the high peaks as blue and white planes, laid on with a broad brush. Here a long ridge streaked with snow runs across the canvas above a dark lake. Pines and a few trees in autumn color grow on the slope at the right.
paintings.setting: The crest of the Sierra Nevada, where ridges above eleven thousand feet hold snow into late summer.
paintings.alt: A long mountain ridge streaked with snow above a dark lake, with pines and orange autumn trees on the slope at right.

paintings.file: Thomas Hill - Great Canyon of the Sierra, Yosemite.jpg
paintings.title: Great Canyon of the Sierra, Yosemite
paintings.blurb: Hill painted this view in 1872, the year after he came back to California from several years in the East. From a high point the valley opens between pale granite walls, with light falling through haze on the far cliffs. Tall pines frame the right side.
paintings.setting: Yosemite Valley in the Sierra Nevada, protected by the state of California from 1864.
paintings.alt: A wide view down a valley between pale granite cliffs in hazy light, tall dark pines framing the right side.

paintings.file: Hetch Hetchy Side Canyon, I, by William Keith, c1908.jpg
paintings.title: Hetch Hetchy Side Canyon, I
paintings.museum: Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco (de Young)
paintings.blurb: Keith painted in the Hetch Hetchy Valley around 1907 and 1908, when his friend John Muir was fighting the plan to dam it for San Francisco's water. A stream runs over pale granite slabs, with trees on the bank and snowy peaks under clouds behind. The dam was approved in 1913, and the valley now lies under a reservoir.
paintings.setting: A side canyon of the Hetch Hetchy Valley in Yosemite National Park, before the O'Shaughnessy Dam flooded it.
paintings.alt: A stream running over pale granite slabs, trees along its bank and snow-capped peaks under white clouds behind.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne Sierra Lake and Peaks.jpg
paintings.title: Sierra Lake and Peaks
paintings.blurb: In this painting gray-blue peaks rise straight up from a turquoise lake, with snow in their gullies. A bright green meadow lines the near shore, and dark pines stand at both sides. Payne painted many such views, using a frame of trees to lead the eye up to the rock.
paintings.setting: A lake basin in the high Sierra Nevada, framed by pines and granite walls.
paintings.alt: Gray-blue mountain peaks with snowy gullies rising above a turquoise lake, a green meadow and dark pines on the near shore.

paintings.file: Alson Skinner Clark, California Mountains.jpg
paintings.title: California Mountains
paintings.blurb: Clark grew up in Chicago, studied with William Merritt Chase in New York and in Paris, and spent 1913 painting the digging of the Panama Canal. After serving in the First World War he settled in Pasadena in 1920 and turned to the California landscape. Here he set gray granite boulders against a bright sky full of moving clouds, with a low line of blue peaks between them.
paintings.setting: The Alabama Hills, a field of weathered boulders in the Owens Valley below Mount Whitney, on the eastern side of the Sierra Nevada.
paintings.alt: Rounded gray boulders on a dry, scrubby slope, low blue mountains behind, and white clouds drifting across a bright blue sky.

paintings.file: California Spring Landscape 1933.4.9 1a.jpg
paintings.title: California Spring Landscape
paintings.museum: Smithsonian American Art Museum, Washington, D.C.
paintings.blurb: Wachtel came to Los Angeles from Maryland in 1882, worked as a violinist as well as a painter, and married the painter Marion Kavanagh in 1904. The two traveled the state together by car to paint. Here a dirt road curves through fields of yellow and orange wildflowers toward a stand of dark trees, with low blue hills behind.
paintings.setting: The valleys of Southern California in spring, when mustard and poppies cover the open fields.
paintings.alt: A dirt road curving through fields of yellow and orange wildflowers toward a clump of dark trees and low blue hills.

paintings.file: Joseph Kleitsch - Laguna Shore Line.jpg
paintings.title: Laguna Shore Line
paintings.blurb: Kleitsch was born in Hungary, made his name as a portrait painter in Chicago and Mexico City, and moved to Laguna Beach in 1920. There he took up landscape. In this painting golden rocks and tide pools fill the foreground, the water is a strong blue, and the cliffs run off along the coast in warm light.
paintings.setting: The tide pools and coves of Laguna Beach, where Kleitsch lived from 1920 until his death in 1931.
paintings.alt: Golden rocks and shallow tide pools in the foreground, a bright blue sea, and sunlit cliffs along the coastline.

paintings.file: Mary DeNeale Morgan Golden Hillside.jpg
paintings.title: Golden Hillside
paintings.blurb: By summer the grass on the hills around Carmel turns gold, and Morgan painted that color across most of this canvas. Dark green trees sit in clumps on the slope, their shapes bent by the wind. Gray hills fade into the distance behind them.
paintings.setting: The hills around Carmel and the Monterey Peninsula in the dry season.
paintings.alt: A golden grassy hillside with clumps of dark, wind-bent trees and gray hills in the distance.

paintings.file: Wendt - The Interview.jpg
paintings.title: The Interview
paintings.museum: Private collection, on loan to The Huntington, San Marino
paintings.blurb: Wendt was a religious man who saw the landscape as the work of God, and he rarely painted people. In this painting two big sycamores lean toward each other, their white trunks and limbs crossing. Patches of light and violet shade cover the ground around them.
paintings.setting: A sycamore grove in Southern California, where these trees grow along creek beds.
paintings.alt: Two large sycamores with white, mottled trunks leaning toward each other, patches of light and violet shade on the ground.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne Sierra Lake, Fifth Lake.jpg
paintings.title: Sierra Lake, Fifth Lake
paintings.blurb: The Big Pine Lakes are numbered from First Lake up the canyon, and Fifth Lake sits high in the chain. Payne painted it with blue peaks and snowfields above a blue lake, a strip of green and gray shore, and a few dark pines in front.
paintings.setting: Fifth Lake, one of the Big Pine Lakes below the Palisades on the east side of the Sierra Nevada.
paintings.alt: Blue mountain peaks with white snowfields above a blue lake, a green and gray shoreline and a few dark pines in front.

paintings.file: Thomas Hill - Indian by a lake in a majestic California landscape.jpg
paintings.title: Indian by a Lake in a Majestic California Landscape
paintings.blurb: This painting has a long descriptive title, given when it sold. Hill set a calm lake between slopes of autumn trees, with a snowy peak far off under a sunset sky. A single tall pine stands at the right, and a small figure rests near the water.
paintings.setting: A lake in the Sierra Nevada at sunset, with snow on the distant peaks.
paintings.alt: A calm lake between slopes of autumn trees, a snowy peak under a sunset sky, a tall pine at right and a small figure by the water.

paintings.file: Land's End by William Keith, 1873.jpg
paintings.title: Land's End
paintings.blurb: Keith painted this view at the western edge of San Francisco in 1873, a year after he met John Muir. Rocky slopes come down to the water, small figures stand on the rocks, and waves break around dark boulders below. Across the water the hills of Marin run off under clouds.
paintings.setting: Lands End, at the northwest corner of San Francisco, looking toward the Golden Gate and the Marin headlands.
paintings.alt: Rocky green slopes running down to the sea, small figures on the rocks, waves on dark boulders and hills across the water.

paintings.file: Guy Rose - The Oak.JPG
paintings.title: The Oak
paintings.blurb: Rose painted this oak in 1916, soon after he settled in Pasadena. The trunk is pale gray and the branches twist outward, with sunlight on the leaves above. Through the trees a strip of blue sea and a palm show in the distance.
paintings.setting: A coastal oak grove in Southern California, with the ocean visible beyond.
paintings.alt: A large oak with a pale gray twisting trunk and sunlit leaves, a strip of blue sea and a palm tree visible beyond.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne Sierra Madre from Mt. Vista.jpg
paintings.title: Sierra Madre from Mt. Vista
paintings.blurb: Payne painted this view in muted browns and violets, looking from a high point across a dry valley to ridge after ridge. A few bare trees with reddish branches stand in the foreground. White clouds rise behind the farthest range.
paintings.setting: The San Gabriel Mountains, once called the Sierra Madre, above the San Gabriel Valley.
paintings.alt: Brown and violet mountain ridges beyond a dry valley, with bare reddish trees in the foreground and white clouds behind.

paintings.file: Edgar Payne Sierra Mountains.jpg
paintings.title: Sierra Mountains
